dedupe_keys.name: understanding the experiences of heat network consumers the social agency for citizens advice may 2025 interviews with 50 households in england scotland and wales

description: This research report, written by The Social Agency (formerly Basis Social) for Citizens Advice and dated May 2025, explores the experiences of 50 domestic heat network customers across England, Scotland and Wales, interviewed between December 2024 and March 2025. The executive summary finds that all participating households had seen heating and hot water bills rise, often doubling or tripling since autumn 2021, and it sets out the drivers of consumer detriment: low awareness of being on a heat network, metering and billing problems, bundling of heat costs with rent, high standing charges for prepayment customers, poorly insulated pipes and frequent breakdowns, retrospective tariff increases and back-billing, and unclear communication and poor customer service. The report also describes effects on finances, health and daily choices. Access: free PDF; no licence is stated, and the interview transcripts are not released, only the findings. Coverage is Great Britain, qualitative and from a small sample. Caveats: only the executive summary was read here, and 50 households cannot represent all heat network customers. It suits resilience and capacity planning studies of heat network service quality and affordability, and no directly related records are catalogued yet.
